notes:
PASS on the fake backend only by python3 -m mhs.driver check (evidence contract_checked, never an MHS-Device level). The package is model-authored and unreviewed (driver.lock.json reviewed_by is null); no hardware was attached and no hardware backend was run.

WHAT IT SERVES: the card's models[0], ksim-kbot/ksim_kbot/kscale-assets/kbot-v2-feet/scene.mjcf, as a MujocoDriver in simulated mode R0. cap.world.step.v1 takes {ticks, action: {ctrl: [...]}}; the bridge derives one control interval per actuator from the loaded model's actuator_ctrlrange (20 motor actuators over the 27 qpos / 26 qvel values: one free joint plus 20 hinges) and checks every element before data.ctrl is written, then mj_step runs ticks times. cap.world.reset.v1 restores the model defaults with mj_resetData + mj_forward. The state is the bridge's integration state (time_ms, qpos, qvel, ctrl, tick, timestep_ms, seed). The card's other model files are not served separately: one package serves one device, and the driver and fake use models[0].

WHY THIS SHAPE: the card's family-config decision and the MujocoDriver helper match the upstream, a MuJoCo training stack for K-Bot. The card lists no entry_symbols, so there was no symbol to verify; the card's five model files exist in the clone. DEVIATION FROM THE CARD: none. The model is read from the read-only checkout and never imported or copied.

WHY A FAKE: MuJoCo is not installed and cannot be installed where the gate runs (no network, no pip), so backends['fake'] is this package's stand-in mujoco module in fake.py (the form the SDK's own MujocoDriver tests use). It expands the scene's robot.mjcf include, resolves the MJCF default classes, and derives the actuator count, the per-actuator control ranges and the joint dimensions from the same text. It loads no mesh, texture or heightfield, resolves no contact, equality, tendon or actuator constraint, and integrates a placeholder velocity proportional to each control value instead of MuJoCo's dynamics; the fidelity gaps list every difference. The real mujoco path (a backend that backends does not name) was not run.

NOT COVERED: MuJoCo itself was never imported, so no trajectory was compared with the real engine; there is no rendering, no mesh/texture/heightfield load, and no contact or friction model. No physical K-Bot is modelled and nothing was validated against the K-Scale hardware. The card's model files live inside the ksim-kbot git submodule, which the pinned superproject commit records as a gitlink (160000 commit), so G4 cannot read a line inside it and no Fact cites one; facts cite README.md, .gitmodules and mechanical/README.md only. The ctrl envelope is derived from the model at run time, not copied into a Limit.

WARNINGS (all expected, none failed): G6.NOT_RECORDED and G7.UPSTREAM_BACKEND because the fake backend is the package's stand-in for the mujoco library rather than a package class the gate can wrap in a Recorder; G8.NO_UNIT x3 for ticks, action.ctrl[*] and seed, the simulator-family inputs the authoring guide lists as expected. No G4.REF_VALUE or G4.REF_BINARY warning was raised, and G1-G5 and G9 passed.

TESTS: test_driver.py keeps mhs.testing.check_driver and adds six cases (model shape from the card model, per-actuator control-range refusals with zero effect, state following the control target, reset to the model defaults, published fidelity contract, e-stop latch); they pass. No operator-required limit, so no site-limits.example.json. No catalogue_requests: the package uses only cap.world.step.v1 and cap.world.reset.v1. check-report.json is regenerated by every gate run and is not part of the package.
